items.explanation: Unique sequential numbers; ties get different numbers.
items.example: SELECT product_name, unit_price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY unit_price DESC) AS rn FROM products LIMIT 5;

items.explanation: RANK leaves gaps after ties, DENSE_RANK does not.
items.example: SELECT product_name, unit_price, RANK() OVER w AS rnk, DENSE_RANK() OVER w AS dense FROM products WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY unit_price DESC) LIMIT 10;

items.syntax: fn() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY col)
items.explanation: Computes the window separately for each group, keeping every row.
items.example: SELECT category_id, product_name, unit_price, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_price DESC) AS rank_in_cat FROM products ORDER BY category_id, rank_in_cat LIMIT 10;

items.syntax: SUM(col) OVER (ORDER BY k ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
items.explanation: Cumulative sum up to the current row.
items.example: SELECT order_id, freight, SUM(freight) OVER (ORDER BY order_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS running FROM orders LIMIT 5;

items.syntax: AVG(col) OVER (ORDER BY k ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
items.explanation: Average of the current and previous two rows.
items.example: SELECT order_id, freight, ROUND(AVG(freight) OVER (ORDER BY order_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS avg3 FROM orders LIMIT 5;
items.expected: First 5 orders with a 3-row moving average.

items.syntax: LAG(col) OVER (ORDER BY k), LEAD(col) OVER (…)
items.explanation: Reads a neighbouring row; NULL (or a default) at the edges.
items.example: SELECT order_id, order_date, LAG(order_date) OVER (ORDER BY order_id) AS prev_date, LEAD(order_date) OVER (ORDER BY order_id) AS next_date FROM orders LIMIT 5;
items.expected: Orders with the previous and next order date.

items.syntax: FIRST_VALUE(col) OVER w, LAST_VALUE(col) OVER (… ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
items.explanation: LAST_VALUE needs a full frame; the default frame ends at the current row.
items.example: SELECT DISTINCT category_id, FIRST_VALUE(product_name) OVER w AS cheapest, LAST_VALUE(product_name) OVER w AS priciest FROM products WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_price ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) ORDER BY category_id;
items.expected: Cheapest and priciest product per category.

items.explanation: An empty OVER () spans all rows.
items.example: SELECT ship_country, SUM(freight) AS f, ROUND(100 * SUM(freight) / SUM(SUM(freight)) OVER (), 1) AS pct FROM orders GROUP BY ship_country ORDER BY pct DESC LIMIT 5;
items.expected: Top 5 countries by share of freight.

items.explanation: Assigns quartiles (or any n buckets) of near-equal size.
items.example: SELECT product_name, unit_price, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY unit_price) AS quartile FROM products LIMIT 8;
items.expected: 8 cheapest products with their price quartile.

items.syntax: WHERE rn <= N on ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY …)
items.explanation: Filter window results in an outer query; WHERE cannot see them directly.
items.example: SELECT * FROM (SELECT category_id, product_name, unit_price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_price DESC) AS rn FROM products) t WHERE rn <= 2;
items.expected: Two most expensive products per category.
